calls.head: The Canadiens hunt better looks than the Sharks
calls.body: The Canadiens wait for good looks, but the Sharks settle for hopeful ones. Montréal is near the top of the league for shot quality, and San Jose is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should be the Canadiens’.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Misa sparks the Sharks back from two down
paras: Montréal had a goal taken off after a video review early in the first. Macklin Celebrini struck first for the Sharks midway through the period, but Nick Suzuki tied it up for Montréal less than three minutes later. Juraj Slafkovský put the Canadiens up 2-1 early in the second. Cole Caufield made it 3-1 midway through the period, but Michael Misa cut Montréal’s lead to 3-2 early in the third. Tyler Toffoli made it 3-3 on the power play midway through the period. Celebrini won it with his second goal of the night on the power play a little over two minutes into overtime. He added an assist for a three-point night.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Canadiens hit two posts and the crossbar twice and came up a goal short. Alex Nedeljkovic made 31 saves for the Sharks, and Jakub Dobeš stopped 26 of 30 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Phillip Danault, even in a loss and with Celebrini’s overtime winner in the game, by our Swing measure.
A scrum midway through the second sent four players to the box. The Sharks moved to 5-4-1, fourth in the Pacific, while the Canadiens dropped to 4-3-2, seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: Cole Caufield scored again against San Jose, and has five goals in seven games against them since 2023-24.
Michael Misa scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 16.
With Alexander Wennberg out, Collin Graf took his spot and won 4 of 6 faceoffs.
The Sharks bounced back after two straight losses.
